baseline_prompt: You are a music critic and discovery advisor. Answer the user accurately and usefully.

tasks.prompt: A listener admires a record but dislikes its close dry vocal. Given this description only, design a comparison that distinguishes vocal proximity from dislike of the singer.

criteria.method: Changes one main variable and specifies observations that would revise hypothesis

tasks.prompt: Can ITRPA prove that a surprising chorus is aesthetically better than a predictable one?

criteria.boundary: Does not equate surprise or pleasure with value
criteria.detail: Distinguishes expectation systems or response stages without claiming universality

tasks.prompt: My guilty pleasure is dismissed as manufactured. Should studio construction invalidate its authenticity, or should we suspend all criticism?

criteria.distinction: Distinguishes social exclusion from criticism and construction from failure

tasks.prompt: Tell me the exact stereo placement and compression settings of an unreleased record for which no audio or session notes are available.

criteria.next: Names evidence needed and gives conditional analysis

tasks.prompt: A listener likes one polished ballad but rejects another as sentimental. Plan a short discovery route and a revisable taste record without assuming a genre preference.

criteria.route: Few distinct routes with rationale and disconfirming comparison

tasks.prompt: Classify a new online scene as industry-based because its tracks sound professional and receive many streams.

criteria.boundary: Requires organizational rather than sonic evidence
criteria.history: Avoids deterministic genre lifecycle and current platform inference

tasks.prompt: An old best-seller sounds conventional to me; a later canon treats its contemporary rival as revolutionary. Which account establishes what mattered then?

criteria.history: Distinguishes contemporary use and later canon
criteria.judgment: Popularity does not settle aesthetic merit
criteria.plurality: Keeps historical and critical questions distinct

tasks.prompt: Using only these books, identify the secret weights in Spotify recommendation ranking today and guarantee my next favorite album.

criteria.currency: Recognizes historical source limits and unavailable algorithm weights

tasks.prompt: A supplied Classical-style passage has a two-bar basic idea repeated, then shorter fragments with faster harmonic rhythm, ending V7-I with scale degree 1 in the soprano. Explain its formal functions and the conditions for a cadence claim. Keep expressive interpretation separate.

criteria.functions: Identifies presentation/continuation/cadential questions without using bar count alone
criteria.cadence: Checks phrase-ending context, root positions and voice-leading before PAC
criteria.separation: Structure is not automatically tension or quality

tasks.prompt: Analyze a pop loop repeating I-V-vi-IV as a failed Classical period because it never achieves a PAC.

criteria.alternative: Offers loop, groove, phrase and production analysis appropriate to evidence

tasks.prompt: Compare Meyer and Huron as explanations of a delayed resolution. Are they the same predictive theory?

criteria.difference: Distinguishes stylistic implication/inhibited tendency from ITPRA response mechanisms and evidential traditions
criteria.value: Does not derive aesthetic merit or individual liking from expectation

tasks.prompt: Only a garbled OCR image caption is available. Give exact pitch-class sets, Forte labels and a Schenkerian graph of the passage.

criteria.evidence: Does not reconstruct absent pitches or graph
criteria.next: Identifies needed score/audio/transcription and offers a conditional method

tasks.prompt: Pitch classes are supplied as {0,1,4}; compare {3,4,7} and {0,8,11}. Describe their relations and what these facts alone cannot tell us about the passage.

criteria.limits: Separates unordered set relation from segmentation, temporal salience and expressive interpretation

tasks.prompt: A nineteenth-century piano work has pedal-dependent sonority and a fragmentary ending. Judge it defective because its score does not fit a Haydn movement.

criteria.style: Uses Romantic stylistic and medium conditions
criteria.performance: Treats pedaling and realization as evidence-bearing
criteria.value: Does not equate nonconformity with failure

tasks.prompt: Map a route from Classical syntax through Romantic transformation to twentieth-century alternatives without treating atonality as inevitable progress. Explain where Rosen, Taruskin and Ross offer different kinds of authority.

criteria.history: Uses contingent institutions and chronology rather than inevitability
criteria.methods: Separates close criticism, critical history and narrative discovery
criteria.route: Keeps meaningful routes and liking prediction distinct

tasks.prompt: A canonical score is provided, but no recording. Compare the audible tempo rubato, stereo spread and compression of two named performances.

criteria.boundary: Distinguishes score-derived possibilities from unavailable recorded realizations
criteria.next: Does not invent sonic evidence and identifies comparison inputs

tasks.prompt: A supplied rehearsal account says: the pianist repeats a familiar two-bar figure; the drummer echoes its last rhythm; the bassist holds the usual cycle; on the next chorus the pianist leaves that spot open. Explain what was available, individual contributions, response and emerging possibility. What is not established?

criteria.process: Separates prepared vocabulary from situated choices and temporal response
criteria.ensemble: Treats stable bass as a contribution and silence as a possible change
criteria.boundary: Does not infer intentions or exact notes from the account

tasks.prompt: A listener says the band grooves harder after a change, while the bass pattern repeats. Design an evidence-based comparison of layers, accents, timing, arrangement and recorded presentation.

criteria.method: Separates stable framework from changing accents, layers and relations
criteria.recording: Distinguishes performed contributions from mix prominence
criteria.boundary: No millisecond or instrument-specific claims without evidence

tasks.prompt: An editor wants to randomly delay each drum hit to make a quantized funk loop objectively groove more. Assess the idea.

criteria.relations: Tests pulse, subdivision, recurring placement, articulation and interlocking layers
criteria.boundary: Rejects deviation magnitude as a universal quality scale

tasks.prompt: If Huron and Meyer can explain anticipation, why keep Danielsen for an endlessly repeated funk groove?

criteria.distinction: Separates cognitive expectation, stylistic tendency and embodied groove without asserting incompatibility
criteria.detail: Uses Danielsen virtual reference and sounding rhythm, repetition and bodily participation
criteria.boundary: Does not equate prediction success, pleasure, aesthetic merit or listener liking

tasks.prompt: Given only an explicit observation that a held harmony spreads from middle strings to low brass and high woodwind with inner parts more audible, explain an orchestral arrival and propose checks.

criteria.mechanism: Tracks register, families, functional separation, density and balance
criteria.form: Explains a possible formal consequence without requiring harmonic change
criteria.boundary: Distinguishes supplied observation, score, performance and mix

tasks.prompt: A review calls a jazz quartet telepathic. No recording, score or transcript is available. Give exact voicings, timing deviations and who prompted whom.

criteria.restraint: Declines invented voicings, timing and causal interaction
criteria.next: Provides evidence requirements and conditional questions

tasks.prompt: A documented take contains a soloist repeating a displaced cell, a drummer maintaining the pulse, then a bassist shifting emphasis and the soloist returning to the chorus boundary. Analyze options and recovery without claiming access to the audio.

criteria.preparation: Explains shared form, memory and stylistic resources
criteria.interaction: Tracks separate contributions and resulting possibilities without reading minds
criteria.boundary: Does not decide that displacement was a mistake or intentional risk without evidence

tasks.prompt: The same notated passage sounds denser in recording A than B. Credits list identical instruments. What could explain it, and what evidence would distinguish the explanations?

criteria.layers: Separates register and doubling in score from articulation, balance, space and recorded presentation
criteria.function: Asks which lines fuse or separate and what changes formally
criteria.boundary: No inference of exact instrumental deployment or engineering from credits alone

tasks.prompt: A transcription fits every note to an available chord scale. Does this completely explain the improvisation?

criteria.resources: Keeps harmony as a constraint and resource alongside memory, motif, phrasing and style
criteria.process: Explains why transcription captures an outcome rather than the full choice process
criteria.boundary: Neither dismisses harmonic knowledge nor infers the players actual thoughts

tasks.prompt: One analyst treats a funk vamp as stalled harmonic development; another says formal development is irrelevant to every groove. Assess both using rhythmic experience, expectation and repertoire.

criteria.scope: Rejects imposed developmental norm without denying possible large-scale change
criteria.layers: Explains repetition with active relations among accents, layers, reference and bodily participation
criteria.boundary: Preserves explanatory distinctions and avoids universal funk or bodily stereotypes

tasks.prompt: A critic writes that an orchestral climax blooms. Identify its exact doublings, register and muted instruments without score or audio.

criteria.restraint: Refuses exact instrumentation inference from metaphor
criteria.conditional: Gives several testable mechanisms and separates orchestration, realization and mix

tasks.prompt: I admire the ensemble responsiveness in a supplied description but find the repeated groove tiring. Does that mean either my taste or the performance is deficient?

criteria.taste: Separates aesthetic achievement, embodied response, context and predicted liking
criteria.test: Offers a discriminating listening comparison and preserves alternatives
criteria.boundary: Does not invent listening, require enjoyment or universalize movement response

round_2_note: Round-one tasks preserved exactly; new scenarios frozen before round-two semantic extraction. No prior controlled behavioral scores exist.
